title: asclepias longifolia var. hirtella
intro: Asclepias longifolia var. hirtella, commonly known as Hairy Green Antelope-horn Milkweed, is a perennial plant species within the Asclepias genus, characterized by its hairy stems, long leaves, and clusters of small, white or yellowish flowers. This plant has been traditionally used to treat various health issues, including fever reduction, sore eyes, and inflammation, due to its potential health benefits in lowering body temperature and relieving pain. The therapeutic actions of Hairy Green Antelope-horn Milkweed are attributed to its anti-inflammatory, antipyretic, and analgesic properties, which help to reduce inflammation and alleviate pain. The bioactive constituents responsible for these effects include alkaloids, glycosides, and terpenoids, which have been identified in various studies as the primary compounds contributing to its medicinal properties.
